misconceptions.description: Assuming m = 2j - 3 guarantees a good truss with no further checks
misconceptions.trigger: learner treats the member-count test as sufficient without inspecting geometry
misconceptions.feedback: The count test is important, but geometry and support layout still matter. A structure can satisfy the count and still be unstable if the arrangement is poor.

misconceptions.description: Forgetting the two-force-member assumption in ideal truss analysis
misconceptions.trigger: learner discusses every truss member as if it carries full beam bending in the ideal statics model
misconceptions.feedback: In the ideal truss model, members are treated as two-force members that carry axial tension or compression only.

misconceptions.description: Assuming zero-force members are always unnecessary
misconceptions.trigger: learner wants to remove any member that is zero under one load case
misconceptions.feedback: A zero-force member under one case may still stabilize the structure, support a different load case, or improve performance during construction.
